resources.name: Global 250-meter Land Cover Dataset
resources.description: The "Belt and Road" monitoring area spans a vast geographical region with diverse land cover types. In 2014, the predominant land cover types within the monitoring area were forest, grassland, and cropland (Figure 2-1), with total areas of 12.7933 million km², 12.3442 million km², and 11.5977 million km², respectively, accounting for 24.07%, 23.22%, and 21.82% of the total area (Table 2-2). In terms of spatial distribution, forests are primarily located in subarctic and tropical zones; grasslands are mainly distributed across the plateau and mountainous regions of Central Asia and northern Russia; croplands are concentrated in areas such as the Indian Peninsula, the Indochinese Peninsula, the Western European Plain, the Central European Plain, and the Eastern European Plain. Additionally, bare land occupies a significant area, accounting for 20.69% of the total monitoring area, and is predominantly distributed across arid regions in Asia and Africa as well as the Mongolian Plateau.

resources.name: Remote sensing carbon loss estimation dataset from global impervious surfaces expansion during 1985-2020
resources.description: This dataset integrates multi-source satellite remote sensing products (including land cover data, biomass data, and surface soil organic matter data) with dynamic global vegetation model simulation outputs (such as net biome productivity data). Following the calculation methodology recommended in the *IPCC 2006 Guidelines for National Greenhouse Gas Inventories*, it quantifies global carbon loss resulting from impervious surface expansion from 1985 to 2020. The dataset comprises five periods: 1985–2000, 2000–2005, 2005–2010, 2010–2015, and 2015–2020. It is stored in .tif format, with a total data volume of 391 MB.

resources.name: Global 1km 8-day Vegetation Leaf Area Index Dataset (2018-2019)
resources.description: Leaf area index (LAI), defined as leaf area per unit area, is an important parameter to characterize vegetation growth. As the key input of dynamic process models such as climate model and carbon cycle model, it is very important to accurately estimate high-quality long-time series Lai products at regional or global scale from satellite remote sensing data. The belmanip station cycles and MODIS leaf area index (LAI) data are fused, and the neural network is trained with the preprocessed MODIS surface reflectance data. Then, based on the preprocessed MODIS surface reflectance data, the global Lai products with a resolution of 1km / 8 days in 2018-2019 are produced. The Lai products produced are complete in space and continuous and smooth in time series. Lai products in 2018 and 2019 are in good agreement with geoarc's thematic data set "land vegetation growth". The data set is divided by sinusidal tile grid, and the longitude and latitude range covered by each scene is 10 ° X10 °. The data set is stored in HDF format.

resources.name: Global 1km Forest Aboveground Biomass Dataset
resources.description: The distribution of forest aboveground biomass in 2014 indicates that Southeast Asia, located at low latitudes, experiences year-round high temperatures and abundant sunlight and precipitation. This region boasts rich forest resources with lush vegetation, primarily consisting of tropical rainforests and tropical monsoon forests. Russia and Europe are home to the world's largest expanse of subarctic coniferous forests, accounting for approximately one-fifth of the global forest area. The forest NPP in Southeast Asia generally exceeds 400 gC/m²·a. Due to relatively poor light and temperature conditions, Russia's forest NPP is only 83.67 gC/m²·a. However, the aboveground biomass in central Russia is significantly higher than in other regions, with enormous forest stock volumes. In contrast, Central Asia, West Asia, and Africa have scarce forest resources.

resources.name: 1 km Resolution Vegetation Growing Season Length Dataset for the China–ASEAN Region
resources.description: The China-ASEAN region is rich in land cover types, including farmland, forest, grassland, shrub and other vegetation types. The length of vegetation growth season determines the effective period of vegetation growth, which is the sum of the effective growth length of each growth cycle in a year. Monitoring the length of vegetation growth season with remote sensing is of great significance for ecological environment protection, soil and water conservation and other applications. The remote sensing data used in this data set are mainly Chinese satellite data, and the sensors used include the China Fengyun 3 Moderate Resolution Spectral Imager (FY3A/B-MERSI) with a spatial resolution of 1 km, the FY3A/B-VIR Visible Light Infrared Scanning Radiometer (FY3A/B-VIR), the Terra/Aqua-MODIS, and so on. The vegetation growth season length product with a spatial resolution of 1 km from June 2013 to May 2014 was obtained. The compressed data volume of this dataset is 6.04MB, and the sharing mode is fully open.

resources.name: China ASEAN 1km Annual Cumulative Vegetation Net Primary Productivity Data Set
resources.description: The China-ASEAN region features rich land cover types, including cropland, forest, grassland, and shrubland vegetation. Vegetation Net Primary Productivity (NPP) reflects the total carbon fixed annually by vegetation through photosynthesis and is a key parameter for assessing vegetation carbon sequestration capacity and carbon budgets. It refers to the organic matter accumulated by green plants per unit time and area, representing the remainder after subtracting autotrophic respiration from the total organic matter produced by photosynthesis, and can be calculated from remote sensing data. Remote sensing monitoring of vegetation NPP is significant for ecological protection, soil and water conservation, and other applications. This dataset primarily uses Chinese satellite data, with sensors including the 1km resolution Fengyun-3A/B Medium Resolution Spectral Imager (FY3A/B-MERSI), Fengyun-3A/B Visible and Infrared Radiometer (FY3A/B-VIRR), and the US Moderate Resolution Imaging Spectroradiometer (Terra/Aqua-MODIS). The resulting product is 1km resolution vegetation NPP data for the period June 2013 ~ May 2014. The compressed dataset size is 22.8MB, with a fully open sharing mode.

resources.name: Global 10 km Land Use Intensity Dataset
resources.description:
The average land use intensity index in the Belt and Road Initiative (BRI) monitoring region is 0.34. Significant regional differences exist in land use intensity; however, areas with high index values generally coincide with regions of dense population distribution. In the Indochina Peninsula, South Asia, Europe, and the Anatolian Peninsula, relatively low elevations and favorable hydrothermal conditions, together with a long history of agricultural cultivation, have resulted in a high proportion of cultivated land and construction land. Consequently, the land use intensity index in these regions is generally above 0.6.
In northern Eurasia, the land use intensity index ranges from 0.4 to 0.6. This region belongs largely to a severely cold climatic zone, where the ecological environment is relatively harsh, leading to comparatively lower levels of land utilization. In contrast, regions such as the northwestern Tibetan Plateau, Central Asia, West Asia, and northeastern Africa receive very limited precipitation. Extensive areas of bare land and deserts dominate these landscapes, and only small areas with irrigation conditions have been developed into cropland. As a result, the land use intensity index in these areas is generally below 0.4.

resources.name: "Belt and Road" Region 25km Destructive Wave Annual Frequency Dataset (2010-2015)
resources.description: The annual frequency of destructive ocean waves along the Maritime Silk Road (the "Belt and Road" initiative) shows significant regional variability in its interannual trend. Areas with the largest increases in frequency are concentrated in the high-latitude westerly wind zones, particularly in the Indian Ocean westerly zone, where the maximum increase reached 18 occurrences. In contrast, regions peripheral to the westerly zones and coastal seas generally experienced a decreasing trend. Notably, the central North Sea saw the most significant decline (4.5 occurrences), while the western Arabian Sea decreased by 4 occurrences. Overall, the Northwestern Pacific, Southwestern Pacific, and Indian Ocean basins are not only hotspots for frequent destructive waves but also exhibit a year-by-year upward trend in occurrence. Among the nine coastal sea areas, the Black Sea and Arabian Sea showed an overall increasing trend, while other seas generally decreased, with minimal changes observed in the Sea of Japan and the Bay of Bengal.

resources.name: 1km Resolution Land Surface Evapotranspiration Dataset for China and ASEAN （Total Evapotranspiration 2013）
resources.description: The China-ASEAN region is located in Southeast Asia. Due to its tropical location and transitional position between Asia and Australia, it holds special significance for research in climate and eco-hydrology. Evapotranspiration is a crucial process in the soil-plant-atmosphere continuum, encompassing both evaporation and transpiration. Evaporation refers to the process where water changes from liquid or solid state to gaseous state, while transpiration is the process by which water is released into the atmosphere through the stems and leaves of plants. Utilizing daily remote sensing products of surface evapotranspiration to analyze the spatiotemporal distribution characteristics of evapotranspiration in the China-ASEAN region in 2013 is of great importance for understanding the region's energy balance, water cycle, and biogeochemical cycles. The remote sensing data used in this dataset primarily consist of Chinese satellite data, with sensors including the 1km spatial resolution Medium Resolution Spectral Imager (FY3A/B-MERSI) and Visible and Infrared Radiometer (FY3A/B-VIRR) from China's Fengyun-3 satellites, as well as the Moderate Resolution Imaging Spectroradiometer (Terra/Aqua-MODIS) from the United States. This resulted in a 2013 surface evapotranspiration product with a spatial resolution of 1km. The dataset is stored in ENVI.img format, with a compressed data size of 81.4 MB, and is fully open for sharing.

resources.name: Urban thermal environment and heat island effect

resources.name: Global 0.05° Vegetation Anomaly Index Dataset during ENSO Events (2010-2020)
resources.description: The Vegetation Anomaly Change Index describes the interannual or seasonal anomalous fluctuations of vegetation after removing long-term trend influences from other factors, such as greenhouse effects. The Global ENSO Event Vegetation Anomaly Change Index Dataset (2010–2020) uses satellite remote sensing data, such as MODIS-derived Leaf Area Index (LAI), as vegetation parameter data. After detrending the vegetation data, the standardized z-score method is applied to extract the Vegetation Anomaly Change Index (VAI). During El Niño and La Niña events within the period, the VAI values are averaged monthly to produce VAI products for these two types of ENSO events. The temporal coverage of the dataset spans ENSO events from 2010 to 2020, with global spatial coverage and a spatial resolution of 0.05° (approximately 5 km). The dataset is stored in geographic projection in *.tif format.

resources.name: Coastline Classification Dataset for Port Cities and Surrounding Areas along the Belt and Road Initiative
resources.description: Ports are one of the key contents of the infrastructure construction of the "the Belt and Road". Based on the Landsat 8 OLI satellite image imaged in 2015, and according to the ecological environment of the 25 port cities along the "the Belt and Road" and their surrounding coastal zones, a sign library for remote sensing visual interpretation of the coastline of important port cities is established. Using the vector mapping function of Arcgis10.0 software, visual interpretation methods are adopted, The location extraction and classification of coastline in 25 important port cities and their surrounding areas; In the process, the coastline is drawn with reference to Google Earth images to ensure that the location and type of coastline can be accurately sketched or interpreted, and finally the vector data of coastline distribution and classification of important port cities along the "the Belt and Road" can be obtained. 25 port cities are Shanghai, Busan, Singapore, Jakarta, Kyaukpyu, Bangkok, Kuantan, Mumbai, Gwadar, Calcutta, Chittagong, Colombo, Doha, Abbas, Jeddah, Dubai, Lisbon, St. Petersburg, Djibouti, Port Sudan, Alexandria, Piraeus, Istanbul, Sydney, Darwin. The coastline is defined by the average high tide line, which is divided into two categories: natural shoreline and artificial shoreline. Among them, the artificial shoreline is also divided into seven types: spur dike, port wharf, reclaimed shoreline, aquaculture shoreline, salt field shoreline, traffic shoreline, and moisture-proof shoreline. resources.name: Dataset of the impact of typical major earthquake disasters on terrestrial vegetation
resources.description: Earthquakes are characterized by sudden onset, unpredictability, severe destructiveness, and a high potential for triggering secondary disasters. Secondary hazards such as landslides and tsunamis induced by earthquakes can cause significant damage to surface vegetation, leading to the deterioration of the ecological environment in affected areas. Studying vegetation damage and recovery in earthquake-stricken regions is of great importance for post-disaster reconstruction, ecological restoration, and the coordination of socio-economic development. Based on the GLASS Leaf Area Index (LAI) product, Fractional Vegetation Cover (FVC) product, global 30m land use data from 2010, and the global disaster events database (EM-DAT), this research investigates changes in terrestrial vegetation and their lagged effects under the influence of earthquake hazards through methods such as time-series analysis and spatial statistical analysis.

resources.name: Daily Surface Melting Dataset of the Antarctic Ice Sheet (1999-2019)
resources.description: The surface melting of the Antarctic ice sheet is a sensitive factor for global climate change and has an important impact on the mass and energy balance of the Antarctic ice sheet. This dataset uses data from microwave radiometers, microwave scatterometers, and regional climate models. Based on the threshold method, the freeze - thaw time series of each data source are obtained. After registration, the Categorical Triple Collocation (CTC) method is used for fusion to obtain the freeze - thaw products of the Antarctic ice sheet from 1999 to 2019. The spatial resolution of this dataset, which is 4.45 km, is higher than that of the published products. Moreover, it combines the advantages of different data sources and can provide the daily surface melting situation of the Antarctic ice sheet during the data period. The data type of this dataset is integer, where 1 represents melting and - 1 represents freezing. The dataset is stored in the .no format, and the compressed data volume is 35.7 MB.

Accurately acquiring the spatiotemporal distribution of the fractional snow cover is of great scientific significance for global and regional meteorological and climate forecasting, hydrological simulation and forecasting, water resource management. resources.name: Global 1 km Net Primary Productivity Dataset (Excluding North America)
resources.description: The total net primary productivity (NPP) of terrestrial grasslands in The Belt and Road region in 2014 reached 0.777 billion tC/a, with significant regional variations. Benefiting from abundant water and heat resources, the Southeast Asian region has a small grassland area but the highest productivity, with an annual NPP of approximately 310 gC/(a·m²), which is much higher than the regional average of 61.92 gC/(a·m²). Due to the frigid climate, the annual NPP of the tundra in northern Russia is less than 10 gC/(a·m²). The Eurasian grasslands generally feature sufficient sunlight and an arid climate, with an annual NPP ranging from 10 to 50 gC/(a·m²). The Qinghai-Tibet Plateau has an annual average temperature generally below 0℃, where alpine meadows and alpine steppes are the dominant grassland types, and the grassland NPP is mainly distributed in the range of 10 to 50 gC/(a·m²).

resources.description: The "Belt and Road" marine areas cover the Western Pacific Ocean, Indian Ocean and Eastern Atlantic Ocean, with complex underwater topography including continental shelves with water depth shallower than 200 m, continental slopes between 200 m and 2000 m, and deep-sea basins deeper than 2000 m. The major navigation channels along the "21st-Century Maritime Silk Road" include the Taiwan Strait, Luzon Strait, Malacca Strait, Karimata Strait, Sunda Strait, Makassar Strait, Torres Strait, Palk Strait, Strait of Hormuz, Bab el-Mandeb Strait, Suez Canal, Mozambique Strait, Cape of Good Hope, Turkish Straits, Strait of Gibraltar, English Channel and Skagerrak Strait. According to geographical and ecogeographical characteristics, 12 sea areas and 13 offshore zones within the "Belt and Road" marine regions are selected, and monthly averaged marine remote sensing products from Aqua/MODIS and HY-1A/B COCTS for 2003–2014 are used to conduct remote sensing monitoring and analysis of the marine ecological environment. The sea areas include the Sea of Japan, Eastern China Seas, South China Sea, Java-Banda Sea, Bay of Bengal, Arabian Sea, Persian Gulf, Red Sea, Mediterranean Sea, Black Sea, North Sea and Baltic Sea.

resources.name: Global 1-km Leaf Area Index Dataset 2014 (GLASS-LAI)
resources.description: The Belt and Road region has complex natural and geographical conditions, with diverse forest, grassland, cropland and other ecosystems that exhibit distinct zonality and large regional differences. The total area of forests, grasslands and croplands is 36,735,200 km², accounting for 69.11% of the total monitored area. In 2014, the total forest area in the Belt and Road terrestrial monitoring region was 12,793,300 km², accounting for 35.10% of the world’s total forest area and 24.07% of the total monitored area, with forest aboveground biomass reaching 14.9503 billion tons. Within the monitored region, the areas with large forest coverage are the Mongolia-Russia subregion, Southeast Asia subregion and Europe subregion, accounting for 49.64%, 27.82% and 14.25% of the total forest area in the whole region, respectively. Among all forest ecosystems, boreal coniferous forests and tropical rainforests rank the first and second in terms of forest area. The former is mainly distributed in Russia and Northern Europe, while the latter is primarily located in Southeast Asia.

resources.name: Finer Resolution Observation and Monitoring – Global Land Cover (FROM-GLC) 2015
resources.description: Remote sensing imagery enables the monitoring of dynamic changes in land cover types, providing accurate information on the current state of ecosystems. This dataset covers the entirety of Asia, Africa, Europe, and Oceania, encompassing over 170 countries and regions. To facilitate regional comparative analysis, the land areas under the Belt and Road Initiative monitoring programme are divided into ten major zones: West Asia, South Asia, East Asia, Southeast Asia, Central Asia, Russia, Oceania, Europe, North Africa, and Southern Africa. The maritime monitoring areas of the Belt and Road Initiative primarily encompass three major oceanic regions: the Northwest Pacific, Southwest Pacific, and Indian Ocean; alongside nine key sea areas including the Sea of Japan, Eastern Chinese Sea, Southern Chinese Sea, Java-Bandar Sea, Bay of Bengal, Arabian Sea, Mediterranean Sea, Black Sea, and North Sea. Remote sensing imagery enables the monitoring of dynamic changes in land cover types, providing accurate information to understand the current state of ecosystems.
